executive_summary: Across FY26, Rashi Peripherals delivered a strong recovery-led growth cycle, with core run‑rate business consistently growing 15–30% excluding large one‑off project deals, supported by PC refresh, AI-led premiumization and price tailwinds. Management demonstrated improving execution discipline—prioritizing ROCE over headline revenue—while selectively stepping back from low-margin large projects in FY26. Margins expanded meaningfully in H2FY26 driven by mix, operating leverage and pricing, with FY26 EBITDA margin reaching ~2.9%. Overall, transcripts reflect improving management confidence, better working capital control, and a clearer capital allocation framework, though reliance on cyclical pricing tailwinds remains a key risk.

evidence.statement: We are evaluating each and every large deal because margins and ROEs are lower now due to competition; careful optimism is our current strategy.
Our aspiration is to grow at 2x the market, but large deals will be taken only after completing execution and collections of previous projects.
We were able to convert price hikes and supply constraints into opportunities and delivered 43% Y-o-Y growth with strong profitability.
FY26 has been the most consequential year in a decade; this is a structural multi-year upgrade cycle, not a one-quarter tailwind.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management guidance shows realism and discipline—targets are conservative, explained repeatedly, and not quietly diluted.

margin_commentary: Across quarters, management consistently emphasized that distribution margins are structurally thin and percentage-based. Margin expansion in FY26 was attributed to favorable product mix (run-rate vs projects), pricing-led operating leverage, and cost discipline rather than structural margin reset. Credibility is high as management repeatedly cautioned against extrapolating peak quarterly margins and anchored expectations around ~2.7–3% EBITDA.
revenue_growth_narrative: Revenue growth narrative evolved from run-rate replacement of prior-year large projects (Q1–Q2) to price- and AI-led acceleration in H2. Management consistently distinguished organic run-rate growth from project-led spikes, highlighting PC refresh, AI PCs, component price hikes, enterprise demand and Tier‑2/3 penetration. Narrative remained coherent and internally consistent.

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Logistics and warehousing constraints in Tier‑2 and Tier‑3 cities causing bottlenecks in fulfillment and after-sales support.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: CEO noted poor infrastructure and limited warehousing creating bottlenecks in B and C cities (Q1FY26).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Working capital intensity and long cash conversion cycles inherent in ICT distribution.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management repeatedly discussed 50–60 day working capital cycle and historic CFO volatility (Q1FY26, Q3FY26).

overall_investment_signal: positive: Strong execution, improving ROCE, disciplined capital allocation and structural demand tailwinds outweigh cyclical pricing risks, though sustainability beyond the price-led supercycle must be monitored.
